newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - As Sept T-bonds retrench, 112-24 eyed.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - As Sept T-bonds retrench, 112-24 eyed.

text.p: Technical analysts said Monday they expect the retracement in U.S. Treasury bond futures to deepen a bit before the larger uptrend reasserts itself.
"Near term, what I'm looking for is for the market to pull back to the 112-24 to 113-00 area," said Nick Kalivas, senior credit market analyst for Refco Inc.
He said the market was likely to find a base in that area from which to launch a new challenge of the recent seven-month highs.
"I think the long-term trend really is still upward," Kalivas said.
September Treasury bond futures reached a 7-1/2-month high of 115-02/32 Thursday, but fell back to finish slightly lower on the day in what technicians call a bearish hook reversal.
The contract currently is trading about a point off that peak.

David Eberhart, market strategist at Optima Investment Research Inc, noted the 30-year cash bond has popped back below 6.50 percent yield resistance, the rough equivalent of 114-18 in September futures using a basis of 154 futures ticks. At midday it was 6.54 percent.
Eberhart also identified 112-24 as his short-term downside target. That level, the high from June 20, had served as key resistance but now reverts to support, he said.
Nearby, 112-25 represents a 25 percent retracement of the three-month upmove that topped Thursday, reinforcing the significance of the area as support, Eberhart said.
But he, too, said the bond market was simply blowing off steam in preparation for another ascent.
"The trend is definitely higher. We're just in a corrective phase here," Eberhart said.
A period of consolidation is to be expected following a gain of four points since June, said Ronald Daino, technical market strategist for Smith Barney Inc.
"To take a little breather here is normal," the analyst said, adding his firm remained "very positive" on the bond market.
Kalivas pointed out that open interest in September bond futures had swelled by more than 100,000 contracts between the end of June and mid-July, suggesting liquidation was in order.
Nonetheless, daily and weekly momentum indicators continue to point upward in support of the bigger trend, Daino said.

Once the market gets past this week's stumbling blocks, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins congressional testimony and the two- and five-year Treasury note auctions, September bonds could test 115-16/32, he said.
